comment: He is an amazing teacher and is very open to meeting outside of class to help with anything. The material itself was pretty difficult, but he made it worth it.

I will definitely be sad to see Dr. Routt go but enjoyed his FYS course nonetheless. While he may assign a lot of readings (some of which would be very dull) he never expected anyone to have read ALL the documents. That being said, discussions definitely require you to have read at least some of the texts. Great lectures and good feedback on papers

Very, very bad teacher never take this class. Avoid at all costs. His lectures are also so dull and monotonous. It's like he pulls up a page of Microsoft Word doc and reads off it, nothing else the entire time, every class. Four big papers and no other HW other than reading like 8 books. He is also a very very hard grader. Please don't take him.

Took him for FYS last fall, and I can say he is a great professor. The subject matter wasn't always fascinating, but he did a good job with lectures and was always willing to help you outside of class. This wasn't my first choice in FYS, but it was still a positive experience

This FYS class was very much not fun, which made it difficult to give such a high rating to Dr. Routt, but he earned it. He made what would have been an unbearable class fun. Lots of the readings were painful, but he didn't necessarily expect you to have finished all of them. One thing of note: his handwriting isn't great

Professor Routt is a really nice and funny guy. He is easy to talk to and is very friendly in and out of class. However, his assignments are often very complicated and hard to understand. He gives a lot of reading, but is very good about breaking it down in class. The essay assignments are long, and the feedback is hard to read and understand.

He's definitely a little dry with his humor, but he understands that most of the students won't be finishing his reading assignments. He's very lecture heavy and is kinda boring at first, but he's grown on me a lot.

I honestly loved this teacher & class! Not going to lie I got stuck with this class last minute & at first was not happy. After taking it I would highly recommend it to others. Though it can be a bit reading heavy at times I felt you can easily do well in this class. I recommend participating a lot & try not to save papers to the last minute!

I took Dr. Routt's Monks and Nuns FYS. This course is NOT for everyone, but for those that have any interest in the workings of medieval Christian history, take this course! He is incredibly knowledgeable and has a dry sense of humor. He can be intimidating at first, but an excellent professor. Use office hours as he gives good feedback on drafts.

Routt is a really fun professor. I am a history minor so I loved the material, though some of my classmates weren't as thrilled. Go to his office hours to talk about your papers and go to his review sessions before tests. Lots of reading but he'll help you figure out which ones are the most important. Participate in class discussions.
Excellent teacher!
I took him for Did Rome Fall, his class is all lecture, but if you need help you can always go talk to him and he is very friendly. I studied a lot and got an A-

he's a fair grader and a good teacher, and he seems to be an endless source of information about Rome, the middle ages, and england.  He tends to be self-deprecating and talks about kentucky alot, which annoyed me for a while but then I got used to it and just zoned out when he went off on tangents. overall a solid history teacher, I recommend him

As a core professor he is pretty boring and grades pretty tough.  He is really helpful and good about grading rough drafts and being available for review sessions outside of class.  He is a nice guy though with a weird sense of humor and funny stories.

Okay guy, acknowledges how much everyone hates core and tries to make the class part as painless as possible.  Papers are graded pretty tough, but if you put in some effort you can get a B.  Helpful with rough drafts and gives you the midterm and final essay topics beforehand.

dont take his early class because you will fall asleep. all he does is lecture, rarely calls on you. knows that no one can do all the reading and is fine with it. go to class because youll be screwed if you dont. he is helpful if you do the work: hell look at your essays vefore theyre are due. all in all not hard if you work hard. work hard for B+
hard class, ridiculous amounts of reading, soooo boring, i do not recommend this class

Great guy, tries to make class fun, but thats a tough task. Lectures all day every day. Ridiculous amounts of reading that you have to prioritize. Overall a relatively easy course. Very interesting if you are into that time in history. Essay grading seems easy, but testing he is more strict.

very tough grader on in-class tests, but not bad on essays. an insane amount of reading is assigned, physically impossible to do it all. tries to spice up class but its pretty boring. you better be a fast writer since he talks a mile a minute and the stuff he says is always on the tests. seems like a good guy, his class is just ok.

Nice guy,tough grader.Discussions based on students' contributions so no comments = zzz.Accepts that many department-selected books are boring but tries his best to make the class interesting.Most everyone gets straight B's on papers.Papers largely discussion based. Make a meeting to discuss drafts, it really helps.Worked my butt off for an A-.

Lots of reading and lectures/discussions in class.  Will do his best to liven up days when the material is boring, likes to enjoy the occasional joke or off-topic discussion.Is a fair grader. If you keep up with the reading as best as you can and try hard on papers, you will do well.Great Prof.
very helpful

As said, the first week seems boring as death, but once the class gets going he actually tries his hardest to make the class interesting.  There's an incredible amount of reading, but not all of it is necessary, and he knows you won't read it all.  Just try hard on the papers.

He's really funny and laid-back, which helps when class is kind of dragging.  He runs it as a dscussion based class.  He lets a lot of discussions go in teh wrong direction sometimes before redirecting it.  The papers are hard but if you pay attention and take notes you can do well on them.

Routt's class was sometimes incredibly boring, but he allows you to basically do whatever you want and he is ready to help at any time, including if you call him at home.  Overall, hes a really good guy who struggles to make the material exciting.  Also, no homework besides 2 papers.

Seems bland and boring at first but once he relaxes and starts making jokes he's great.  Not only does he actually make Rome interesting, he throws in personal bits that keep everyone focused.  Lots of reading but provides very clear outlines for notes.  Lets you know exactly what he wants.
Absolutely hilarious with his self-deprecating humor!  Hard papers but the class atmosphere is laid-back and relaxed.
He's a fairly nice teacher who is very knowledgable in his field.  Expect to work hard, however, for a B.

He is a good prof overall. He is very funny and definitely relates with students. He is helpful out of class as well as in class and understanding the material. Papers are hard and dont expect an easy A.

He is a good guy who makes jokes he does what he can to liven up the material, but he assigns an inordinant amount of reading at times. He is a somewhat difficult but fair grader. A pretty good prof overall.
He is just one hell of a teacher.  Incredibly helpful, funny, very fair grader, makes learning 1,000 years of history enjoyable and interesting.
